I

He disappeared in the dead of winter: The brooks were frozen, the airports almost deserted, And snow disfigured the public statues; The mercury sank in the mouth of the dying day. What instruments we have agree The day of his death was a dark cold day.

Far from his illness The wolves ran on through the evergreen forests, The peasant river was untempted by the fashionable quays; By mourning tongues The death of the poet was kept from his poems.

But for him it was his last afternoon as himself, An afternoon of nurses and rumours; The provinces of his body revolted, The squares of his mind were empty, Silence invaded the suburbs, The current of his feeling failed; he became his admirers.

Now he is scattered among a hundred cities And wholly given over to unfamiliar affections, To find his happiness in another kind of wood And be punished under a foreign code of conscience. The words of a dead man Are modified in the guts of the living.

But in the importance and noise of to-morrow When the brokers are roaring like beasts on the floor of the Bourse, And the poor have the sufferings to which they are fairly accustomed, And each in the cell of himself is almost convinced of his freedom, A few thousand will think of this day As one thinks of a day when one did something slightly unusual.

What instruments we have agree The day of his death was a dark cold day.

II

You were silly like us; your gift survived it all: The parish of rich women, physical decay, Yourself. Mad Ireland hurt you into poetry. Now Ireland has her madness and her weather still, For poetry makes nothing happen: it survives In the valley of its making where executives Would never want to tamper, flows on south From ranches of isolation and the busy griefs, Raw towns that we believe and die in; it survives, A way of happening, a mouth.

III

Earth, receive an honoured guest: William Yeats is laid to rest. Let the Irish vessel lie Emptied of its poetry.

In the nightmare of the dark All the dogs of Europe bark, And the living nations wait, Each sequestered in its hate;

Intellectual disgrace Stares from every human face, And the seas of pity lie Locked and frozen in each eye.

Follow, poet, follow right To the bottom of the night, With your unconstraining voice Still persuade us to rejoice;
May 24, 2015 - W.H. Auden, *In Memory of W.B. Yeats*

Bug report. Probably a low priority fix - I don't see this flaw being abused that much but still wanted to report a potential flaw anyway.

I was able to ban myself from my own sub while still keeping all mod powers. This made me unable to vote, submit comments or post there while still keeping all mod functions. Commenting while banned gave an unhelpful "you're doing too much, try again later" error. I am able to simply remove myself from the sub banlist so no permanent harm done with this flaw. And, the fact that I could undo my own ban makes this an obvious bug.

I think this could cause trouble if my account is ever compromised, and also lend to petty abuse or trolling other co-mods. Sure there are plenty of other ways to cause trouble and far worse than this, but this is just one way I thought about and tested.

Really if a sub owner wants to ban an abusive or unwanted co-mod, steps would be a) remove that mod from the modlist, then b) ban them.

Edit: Suggested fixes:

1) If a mod adds their own self to the sub banlist, reply with a 418 "Are you insane?" error message and stop processing the request.

2) If a mod adds another co-mod to the sub banlist and has the proper authorization according to any related Voat rules, show a confirmation message "This will remove the user from the modlist and ban them from this sub. Are you sure?" On "OK", continue removing the user from the modlist and then add them to the sub's banlist.

I am an average citizen from Norway. AMA
What's one thing people fail to understand about Norway that annoys you?
Hah, what? Not sure what could annoy me, but I guess it's quite silly that people think of Norway as this special fairy tale country. It's basically the same as Canada or anywhere North.
How do you feel about the other Nordic countries?
We're all basically the same. I feel like Norway is a bit more conservative than Sweden and Denmark though.
I have brown hair. Blonde hair is less common than you'd think actually.
My dog makes a "Boff" sound when he barks. Some others I've heard make either a high pitch "arf" sound or a "waoff" sound.

My father's side of our family immigrated to the U.S. from Norway. His parents were the first of his family to be born in the U.S. They first settled in Minnesota, and then moved into Iowa. The only Norwegian dish that our family eats is a potato dish that we call kumla. In Minnesota they call it kloob, or klub. It's essentially a very dense and heavy potato dumpling. In Minnesota it's served with ham, but our family does it with pork shoulder. We poach a pork shoulder roast and reserve the poaching liquid. We grate potatoes and mix with flour and salt to make a very stiff dough. We then drop large spoonfuls of the dough into the pork broth to poach. The pork shoulder is shredded and fried up in butter. The potato dumplings and pork are served with more melted butter to pour over and salt and pepper if desired. A relish plate of pickles and olives is passed as an accompaniment. So, does Norway have an authentic dish that resembles this dish that I'm told is Norwegian? If you do, then how close is our version to authentic?

Ah yeah, that's usually called "Raspeball". I've never tasted it myself, but I've heard it's quite good.

There's even a wiki page for it http://no.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raspeball or http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raspeball

It's more of a west-norwegian thing.

Taco is really popular where I live, and a lot people eat it once a week. We also have like 100 kebab/sushi/chinese restaurants scattered about everywhere. Not so much traditional food here anymore, except for in gatherings or holidays.

Thanks for the reply. I forgot that a while back we were host to an elderly Norwegian gentleman, and we made this for him. He called it raspekake. And his version was different from ours.

On another note; what do think about Norwegian black metal? Are those guys as evil as it seems, or is it all for show?

Haha, norwegian black metal artists are sweethearts. You'd have a hard time finding someone who isn't nice. I don't personally like black metal, but my brothers and cousin like it a lot.

My cousin even used to sing in a band and he's the most awesome person I know :)

Yes. I've got a distant relative in Norway who is in a black metal band. At the moment I cannot remember, but I'll ask my mom in the morning and check back in. She's met him, and said the same thing: he's a sweetheart and one of the nicest guys you'll meet.
The metal community is generally one of the nicest ones. They all genuinely enjoy making their music, and respect each other. Not sure why so many nice people are attracted to that kind of music.
no idea, probably just a joke on the fact its a lesbian shoot.

I was incredibly surprised when I bought this game, because it is pretty much a complete 180 reversal from the other Borderlands games. There's no insane shoot 'em ups. No tactical builds, or constant death when things get too hairy. It's far more subtle.

To me, it felt slow paced until I realised just what the game was trying to do, let me build up this world in whatever way I wanted, and showing me the world of Pandora through every NPC's eyes ever, rather than the raging roid monster that the vault hunters are. Especially after introducing Zero, I thought you got a feel for how unstoppable these lunatics are.

All in all, I thought it was a great game. The dialogue is funny, charming, and even emotional at times. The voice acting is superb, and there is both a relaxed feeling of watching this story play out in front of you, mixed with a constant state of alertness, because at any point you might need to be quick on the draw and dodge a giant rampaging skag with a taste for Hyperion lackeys. I've never played a game like this.
